title: ～上で — “after ～ing / upon ～”
summary: A formal way to say “after doing ～ (carefully), then ～.” It attaches to a verb ta-form or noun + の, and the main clause is the next step taken on that basis. Common in business, contracts and polite requests.

body.p: A is a necessary preparation such as thinking, reading, discussing or checking. B is the decision or action that follows it. The pattern stresses that B is done on the basis of A.
It sounds careful and formal: よく読んだ上で、サインしてください. Nouns often are action nouns: 相談の上で, 確認の上で (also 御確認の上). Everyday casual speech usually uses ～てから or ～たあとで.
～てから only shows time order. ～上で adds “having done it properly first, and using that result.” It cannot be used when A is not a real step to prepare for B.

examples.ja: よく考（かんが）えた上（うえ）で、お返事（へんじ）します。
examples.romaji: Yoku kangaeta ue de, henji shimasu.
examples.tr: I’ll reply after thinking it over carefully.

examples.ja: 契約（けいやく）の内容（ないよう）をよく読（よ）んだ上（うえ）で、サインしてください。
examples.romaji: Keiyaku no naiyou o yoku yonda ue de, sain shite kudasai.
examples.tr: Please sign only after reading the terms of the contract carefully.

examples.ja: みんなで相談（そうだん）した上（うえ）で、結論（けつろん）を出（だ）そう。
examples.romaji: Minna de soudan shita ue de, ketsuron o dasou.
examples.tr: Let’s reach a conclusion after we all discuss it.

pitfalls: Use the ta-form (読んだ上で), not the dictionary form. The preceding step must already be done.
It is formal. In casual talk, ～てから is more natural.
